decisions.quote: Recent GWAS reports have revealed a novel variant rs1042725 in HMGA2 for human adult height in the European populations.( Lettre et al. , 2008 , Weedon et al. , 2008 , Weedon et al. , 2007 ) Replication of GWAS findings can be quite difficult, especially for the quantitative trait. In this study, we successfully replicated this finding both in the unrelated and family-based US Caucasian populations, which demonstrated the validity of the initial finding.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In 78b62459579bc203 (Yang et al., 2010), the authors explicitly frame their study as an independent replication of the HMGA2 rs1042725 association with adult height reported across three European GWAS—Weedon et al. (2007), Lettre et al. (2008), and Weedon et al. (2008)—noting in the Introduction that 'these studies are performed by the same groups, and the samples are mainly from northern Europe. Replications in multiple additional populations by independent groups are needed to evaluate the credibility and generality of this finding.' In both Results and Discussion, the authors directly compare their empirical replication results (direction of allele effect and statistical significance in unrelated and family-based US Caucasian cohorts) against all three GWAS citations together. Under the codebook rules (including replication chains, where subsequent primary GWAS reports in the chain that are directly retested are valid targets), Lettre et al. (2008) (Nat Genet 40:584-591, DOI 10.1038/ng.125) is a distinct primary empirical study from shipped row 662 (Weedon et al., 2007, Nat Genet 39:1245-1250, DOI 10.1038/ng2121) and is genuinely missing from the shipped rows.

decisions.quote: Therefore, we set out to measure both implicit adaptation and its retention via spontaneous recovery in a single force-ﬁeld paradigm in both healthy young and older adults to test four different hypotheses, reﬂecting previous research: 1) implicit adaptation levels at the end of the adaptation period are similar across age groups (27), 2) spontaneous recovery is larger in young than in older participants (37), 3) implicit adaptation at the end of the adaptation period is correlated with the amount of spontaneous recovery (45), and 4) as suggested by Trewartha and colleagues, spontaneous recovery is related to explicit memory processes such as working memory capacity.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In 7b36096465800442 (Hermans et al., 2025), the authors explicitly design their force-field adaptation study in healthy young (n = 28) and older (n = 20) adults to empirically test four hypotheses reflecting prior research, where Hypothesis 1 is: '1) implicit adaptation levels at the end of the adaptation period are similar across age groups (27)'—citing Reference 27, Vandevoorde & Orban de Xivry (2019) (Neurobiol Aging 80: 138-153, DOI 10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2019.03.020). They preregister and execute dedicated statistical tests for Hypothesis 1 (Analyses 1, 2, and 3 in Statistical Analysis and Results) and conclude in Results and Discussion that implicit adaptation does not deteriorate with age, confirming Vandevoorde & Orban de Xivry (2019). Only Reference 37 (Trewartha et al., 2014, DOI 10.1523/jneurosci.1489-14.2014, row 2324) was shipped. Note that Luna's mechanical quote validation error occurred only because Luna normalized author initials ('J-J.' instead of 'JJ.') and ligatures in the reference quotes; the substantive omission is fully verified in the source text.

corrected_value.title: Can uniform color color aggression? Quasi-experimental evidence from professional ice hockey

decisions.location: Study III Introduction (lines 456-470); Study III Results (lines 595-647); Study III Discussion (lines 651-652); General Discussion (line 678); References (line 752).
decisions.quote:
There is only scant evidence to support the black-aggression hypothesis in the modern NHL ranks. Similar to our previous investigations, we failed to detect the effect when we conducted a nuanced analysis of the overall data (i.e., when accounting for the nested nature of the data) and also when we conducted a team-by-team analysis separately.
Also, we failed to find support for reduced aggression when wearing white uniforms (Webster et al., 2012) as we conducted comparisons within teams across eight seasons while ensuring the overall aggression in the league remained consistent (thus avoiding a history threat).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In Study III of 7bdaa130567dec72 (Goldschmied, Raphaeli, & Furley, 2026), 'Study III: Replication of National Hockey League Black Uniforms Effects in the Modern Era', the authors trace the NHL archival replication chain from Frank & Gilovich (1988) through Caldwell & Burger (2011) to Webster, Urland, & Correll (2012) (DOI 10.1177/1948550611418535). Study III directly retests Webster et al.'s (2012) NHL findings in an 8-season modern NHL dataset (2016/17-2023/24, 71,513 infringements), adopting Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) regression to account for nested team/season observations as emphasized by Webster et al., and explicitly testing both the black-uniform aggression hypothesis and Webster et al.'s (2012) specific finding of reduced aggression in white uniforms ('Also, we failed to find support for reduced aggression when wearing white uniforms (Webster et al., 2012) as we conducted comparisons within teams across eight seasons while ensuring the overall aggression in the league remained consistent'). Under the codebook rules (both as the closest study in the NHL replication chain and for its distinct white-uniform reverse effect), Webster et al. (2012) is a retested target distinct from shipped row 2625 (Frank & Gilovich, 1988). Luna's mechanical quote check failed only because of invisible zero-width spaces (U+200B) in the reference list DOI URL.

corrected_value.title: Androgen receptor splice variants determine taxane sensitivity in prostate cancer

decisions.location: Abstract (lines 94-110); Introduction (lines 144-166); Results and Discussion (lines 330-450); References (line 532).
decisions.quote: Thadani-Mulero and colleagues reported that ARv567 and ARv7 responded differently to docetaxel in their 2014 Cancer Research paper. They found that the ARv567 variant was heavily associated with microtubules, while the ARv7 variant was not, which resulted in a significant decrease of nuclear accumulation of ARv567 but not ARv7 with docetaxel treatment. They performed a xenograft tumor growth assay on two different prostate cancer cell lines: LuCaP 86.2, which expresses wild-type androgen receptor (AR) and ARv567, and LuCaP 23.1, which expresses wild-type AR and ARv7. They reported that docetaxel treatment reduced tumor growth significantly in tumors derived from LuCaP 86.2 cells, while tumors derived from LuCaP 23.1 did not show tumor growth reduction, suggesting that docetaxel affects the AR splice variants differently.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. The paper 7c729ad77091cc25 (Shan et al., 2018, PeerJ, DOI 10.7717/peerj.4661) is a Replication Study from the Prostate Cancer Foundation-Movember Foundation Reproducibility Initiative. The single shipped row (input_row_index 1162, Shan et al., 2015, 'Registered report: androgen receptor splice variants determine taxane sensitivity in prostate cancer', PeerJ, DOI 10.7717/peerj.1232) is the replicating authors' own Stage 1 Registered Report protocol describing their planned methodology, not the original empirical study whose findings are tested. Per the codebook rule ('Before naming any entry, rule out: another work by the same authors; a registered-report protocol or preregistration versus the paper reporting the original finding'), the actual original study being empirically replicated is Thadani-Mulero et al. (2014) ('Androgen receptor splice variants determine taxane sensitivity in prostate cancer', Cancer Research 74:2270-2282, DOI 10.1158/0008-5472.can-13-2876), specifically Figures 6A and 6B (xenograft tumor growth response to docetaxel in LuCaP 86.2 and LuCaP 23.1 prostate cancer lines and Western blot analysis of AR splice variants). Because only the 2015 protocol was shipped, the true original empirical target Thadani-Mulero et al. (2014) is genuinely missing. (Luna's mechanical quote validation error was due to collapsing XML line breaks around inline citations in the text extract.)
